policy: Donor files were read at their pinned commit in the local mirror (tools/mirrors.py), as data; nothing was run. Ideas only, in westack's own words; no donor text is copied (skills/westack/provenance/RIGHTS.md). The component classification is skills/westack/provenance/absorption.json (gstack.health).

usefulness_legend.strong: shaped the skill's structure or its numbers
usefulness_legend.useful: added a rule or a check

sources.read: whole template (stack detection, running tools, the rubric and weights, composite, dashboard, history, trend, recommendations, rules)

taken.mechanism: A declared Health Stack section in the instruction file that wins over detection, and detection from files and PATH that runs nothing.
Each tool run on its own with its full log, its own exit code and counts parsed from the whole log; a failing tool never stops the next; capture failures are errors, never clean or skipped.
The rubric: typecheck 22, lint 18, tests 28, dead code 13, shell 9, each on 10, 7, 4 and 0 bands, with skipped weight redistributed in proportion and partial coverage named.
History compared only with a run of the same coverage, declining categories named, and recommendations ranked by weight times deficit.
Report-only: never fix; the user decides what to act on.
An index category of weight 10 from the index doctor's verdict: ok 10, warnings 7, anything else 0; no index at all is skipped and its weight shared out.

rejected: The gbrain sub-score's queue length and hours since the last push: westack's index has neither; only the doctor verdict is taken, from westack-onboard.
Running the composite through bun: the helper computes it in Python.
A non-zero test exit scoring 4 without counts, and exit 0 scoring 10 without counts: westack scores tests without counts at most 7, and zero executed tests 0.
Persisting the Health Stack to CLAUDE.md as one of three options: here it is a question that needs an instruction-file grant.
gstack's state directory for history: history goes where the user says.
